knownRisks: L-01 - This is a static, source-level check, not a runtime observation. Zero call sites is strong evidence for zero requests, but AC-22, AC-23 and AC-24 are written against the browser network panel and storage inspector. That browser-tier evidence is WS-10's under GATE-AUTOMATED-TESTS and is not claimed here.

L-02 - The scan covers src/ only, which is the whole of what the browser loads (ADR-005 section 1: no build step, the source is the running artifact). tests/ and dev-time tooling are outside this determination; tests/tools/static-server.mjs is a test-time process, not part of the game.

L-03 - Comment text names the very APIs it disclaims, so a naive grep of src/ returns 15 hits that reduce to zero executable occurrences. A reviewer must apply the comment strip or the source-hygiene tier before concluding anything.

L-04 - window.dinoDash deliberately widens the page's global surface (ADR-003 section 4). It is read-only, side-effect free and not keyboard-reachable, so it is an observation surface and not an integration point, but it is the one globally reachable name the delivery adds; a later unit adding a setter would convert it into an attack surface.

L-05 - Client-side score forgeability is already accepted by the owner in DEC-20260809-001, bounded to Units 1 and 2, with server-side validation required from Unit 3 and to be decided at Unit 3. Recorded as inherited context; ENG-04 does not re-accept it.

L-06 - AC-24 governs the running game, not the toolchain. A future clean-checkout install step (npm ci plus a Playwright browser download) touches the network at install time. WS-01 B-01 and ADR-005 section 4 require the install command and the test command to be stated as distinct steps or a verifier will read the evidence as self-contradictory.

L-07 - not_applicable is scoped to Unit 1 at revision bf5ac18. Units 2 through 5 are not contracted and nothing in this record pre-clears them. Unit 3's needs from ENG-04 are stated in the document as open questions only: a submission contract, a server-side validation position, an identity decision that does not exist yet, the fact that endedAt carries no local offset, and the live AC-19 interpretation risk that Z may be read as insufficient against a numeric offset - one formatting function in Unit 1 but a data migration once a server persists it.

L-08 - ENG-04 owns none of AC-22 to AC-25; WS-01 section 3 assigns them to WS-03 with WS-09 and WS-10 contributing. The per-AC findings in the document are domain review findings, not dispositions. Only ENG-15 at WS-14 issues the delivery's verification disposition.
